bridge: Builds on G02 privacy, I03 retrieval scopes and S03 data protection.
teaching:
AI privacy includes what enters prompts, training, retrieval, logs and provider retention. Avoid sending data the task does not need. A confidentiality instruction does not replace an access control or a provider processing agreement. User notes can contain sensitive material even when the application did not explicitly request it.

Redaction can reduce exposure but has false negatives and may remove useful context. Test its boundaries with synthetic examples and keep identity/ownership checks independent. Model memorisation and membership inference are different threat questions from an ordinary logging leak; neither is resolved merely by hiding a UI field.

Define data flows and retention for every copy, including generated summaries, embeddings, caches and traces. Embeddings are not automatically anonymous. Where legal requirements matter, use current authoritative jurisdiction-specific guidance. The native exercise contains only invented identifiers and requires no provider uploads.
example:
Synthetic record
user=A; email=learner@example.invalid; note="review chapter3";
secret_marker=DEMO-DO-NOT-SEND
Task: suggest a study schedule from chapter completion.
Needed: completed chapter IDs and available study time.
Unneeded: email, secret_marker, private free-text notes.
Safe fixture payload: {"completed":[1,2],"minutes":30}
explanation: The strongest reduction here is not sending unnecessary fields in the first place. A redactor that misses a secret marker then has less work to fail at. A real data-flow record must also include who receives the permitted payload and how long it is retained.
exercise: Create a source-to-destination inventory for the supplied task. Include application storage, model provider, logs and user display. Decide permitted fields and retention purpose for each. Identify two derived artifacts needing the same privacy review.
solution: The schedule task needs chapter/time information only under this fixture. Embeddings, cached responses and summaries can retain information derived from private inputs. Do not label them harmless solely because their format differs from the original note.
challenge: A provider setting excludes prompts from training but retains operational logs temporarily. Explain why “not trained on” and “not stored” are different claims, and propose what documentation a deployment owner must verify.
challenge_solution: Confirm retention, access, region, subprocessors and deletion terms for the actual service/account configuration. Training exclusion does not imply zero retention. Keep any personal-data legal conclusion tied to the relevant authority and contract.
